title: A Preregistered Audit of Dataset Contamination Controls in LLM-for-NetOps Benchmarks
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory audit (study_id = contamination-audit-netops-2026-v1) to evaluate whether conservative deterministic contamination detectors (exact normalized token equality, fuzzy 5-gram overlap, provenance heuristics) flag items in a reproducible 150-item NetOps sample and whether applying preregistered guarded exclusions changes validator-based success rates. The preregistration listed four public OpenAlex benchmark targets (https://openalex.org/W7157506260, https://openalex.org/W4404602270, https://openalex.org/W4404534210, https://openalex.org/W7166900660) and froze detectors, thresholds, sampling, and the primary estimand (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline). The executed run, however, sampled provenance-stable synthetic tasks (source_identifier prefix "synthetic-netops:") from a deterministic generator and used shared_initial_candidate generation semantics (independent_condition_generation = false), causing one shared model generation per item to be reused across baseline and guarded episodes. Because no preregistered high-confidence contamination flags occurred, no guarded exclusions or replacements were applied: baseline = 150/150 pass, guarded = 150/150 pass, paired difference = 0.0 percentage points (95% bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.0]); exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. We explicitly classify the primary confirmatory estimand as degenerate/untestable for detecting generation-level contamination under these executed semantics. Using artifact-grounded reconciliation (preregistration SHA-256 = 9a5e11c5b2b1c14c2a4a874a7ad0b9f215f8477a7becf4eb6dd1c0ff6a00ae7a; executed task manifest: execution/task_manifest.jsonl, SHA-256 = b7c08599e3f96d8d5605a18f8f973e0707d7224327eeed7bde78c0d34cb83e55; model configuration: execution/model_configuration.json, SHA-256 = a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820), we diagnose why the run was uninformative for web-sourced contamination and recommend concrete artifact-anchored design changes (provenance-rich public sampling, independent_condition_generation = true, persist full per-item overlap scores, multi-model replication, paraphrase-robust detectors) to make future audits sensitive to contamination in public benchmarks. All primary artifacts and validator traces are archived and cited in the Disclosure Statement.

sections.introduction:
Motivation. Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to translate high-level network intent into concrete device configurations and to propose automated repairs. Operational trust in LLM-driven NetOps depends on valid evaluations: measured success must reflect model capability, not dataset contamination (items or templated prompts present in model training data) or low-complexity task artifacts. Surveys and recent benchmark analyses call for contamination-aware evaluations that combine deterministic fingerprinting, fuzzy n-gram overlap, provenance tracing, and verifier-based oracles.

Research question and contribution. We preregistered a confirmatory audit to answer: under conservative deterministic contamination detectors (exact-match + fuzzy 5-gram + provenance heuristics) and a preregistered guarded exclusion policy, how many high-confidence contamination flags arise in a reproducible 150-item NetOps sample drawn from prespecified benchmark candidates, and how much does applying those controls change a validator-based success rate for a hosted LLM? The preregistration explicitly listed four public OpenAlex benchmark targets (https://openalex.org/W7157506260, https://openalex.org/W4404602270, https://openalex.org/W4404534210, https://openalex.org/W7166900660) and froze detectors, thresholds, sampling, and the primary paired estimand (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline). Our contributions are: (1) a fully preregistered confirmatory experiment (preregistration SHA-256 = 9a5e11c5b2b1c14c2a4a874a7ad0b9f215f8477a7becf4eb6dd1c0ff6a00ae7a) executed end-to-end and archived; (2) exact, artifact-verified confirmatory statistics on Npairs = 150 with deterministic validator traces; (3) an explicit preregistration→execution reconciliation that documents why the execution produced a degenerate null for generation-level contamination and prescribes artifact-grounded corrective design changes.

Scope and bounded claims. The audit targeted the methodological question of whether the preregistered conservative detectors and guarded policy would alter validator-measured success in a reproducible sampling and generation regime. The executed sample comprised provenance-stable synthetic tasks (source_identifier prefix "synthetic-netops:") generated deterministically and the pipeline used shared_initial_candidate generation semantics (independent_condition_generation = false). These executed facts, recorded in execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA-256 = b7c08599e3f96d8d5605a18f8f973e0707d7224327eeed7bde78c0d34cb83e55) and execution/model_configuration.json (SHA-256 = a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820), limit inference: the observed zero-flag, zero-difference outcome applies to this synthetic shared-generation regime and does not imply absence of contamination in independently sampled public benchmarks.
sections.related_work:
LLM-driven NetOps and verification. Prior work shows that LLMs can generate configuration artifacts from intent and that generate–validate–repair loops (LLMs plus verifiers) improve average repair quality versus naive generation. Formal and deterministic verification tools (Header Space Analysis, NetPlumber-family approaches) are established oracles for reachability and policy correctness and are suitable for automated generate–validate pipelines. Recent benchmarks and systems (e.g., agentic configuration-repair studies and Astragalus-style systems) document both promise and per-case regressions, motivating defenses.

Evaluation‑validity critiques and contamination detection. Surveys and meta-analyses emphasize two recurrent risks: dataset contamination (inclusion of benchmark items or templates in model training corpora) and construct invalidity (benchmarks dominated by templated, low-complexity items). Recommended defenses include exact normalized fingerprinting, fuzzy n-gram overlap detectors, provenance timestamp checks, and conservative replacement/exclusion rules. Our audit implements a conservative subset of these defenses with a deterministic guarded exclusion policy and a deterministic validator oracle; unlike broad capability leaderboards, our manuscript focuses on whether those preregistered defenses, when applied in a reproducible pipeline, change validator-based success on a frozen confirmatory sample.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and frozen design. The study was preregistered as contamination-audit-netops-2026-v1 (preregistration SHA-256 = 9a5e11c5b2b1c14c2a4a874a7ad0b9f215f8477a7becf4eb6dd1c0ff6a00ae7a). The preregistration specified: primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; confirmatory sample size = 150 items (50 per dataset when available) drawn from the four public OpenAlex benchmarks listed above; detectors = (1) exact normalized token equality, (2) fuzzy 5-gram shingle overlap with preregistered high-confidence threshold ≥ 0.80, and (3) provenance timestamp heuristics; guarded policy = deterministic exclusion and deterministic replacement for high-confidence flags; analysis = paired_binary_analysis_v1 (exact McNemar two-sided test + paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI with 10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729). The preregistration also allowed deterministic synthetic sampling when public sampling was infeasible.

Execution semantics and determinism. The execution used deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 to deterministically generate the confirmatory sample; per-task generator seeds and source provenance are archived in execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA-256 = b7c08599e3f96d8d5605a18f8f973e0707d7224327eeed7bde78c0d34cb83e55). The declared model was gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json: requested_model = "gpt-5-mini", independent_condition_generation = false; file SHA-256 = a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). The executed pipeline used shared_initial_candidate semantics: a single generation per item was reused for baseline and guarded episodes unless a high-confidence contamination flag triggered exclusion/replacement. This choice reduced model calls (model_calls_used = 150) relative to the preregistered maximum (300) and mechanically collapses baseline vs guarded discordance when no exclusions occur; these counts and reconciliation are recorded in the execution manifest and deterministic_reconciliation artifacts.

Contamination detectors and persistence policy. The preregistered detector suite implemented deterministic heuristics: (1) exact normalized token equality; (2) fuzzy 5-gram shingle overlap with preregistered high-confidence flag when overlap ≥ 0.80 (with sensitivity brackets at 0.65 and 0.50); and (3) provenance timestamp heuristics comparing item timestamps/DOIs to public archive cutoffs. The detector workflow was implemented to persist detailed per-item overlap tables only when threshold crossings or replacements occurred (this persistence policy is recorded in the transformation manifest: execution/transformation_manifest.json; see full execution bundle for the transformation artifact and its hash manifest). This storage-saving behavior explains the archived absence of a global per-item overlap table when no threshold crossings were observed.

Guarded exclusion and deterministic replacement. The preregistered guarded policy excluded only high-confidence flagged items (exact match OR fuzzy overlap ≥ 0.80) and deterministically replaced them with retemplated deterministic augmentations sampled from the same generator subject to an embedding-similarity intent-preservation safeguard (preregistered minimal cosine ≥ 0.85). Replacement traces and retemplating artifacts would be archived when they occur; because no high-confidence flags occurred in this run, no replacements were performed and analysis/contamination_summary.csv is empty (SHA-256 = 389227f0d1e81239c7498abd4944a04c59c92c5fa042b990e332796cd61c3222).

Deterministic validator and scoring. The verification oracle was deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version = 5.0). For each candidate the validator parsed commands, applied them to an explicit device/state model, and checked task-specific final-state and workflow constraints. The preregistered scoring rule full_intent_constraint_validation required final-state matching on allowed fields and respect of workflow transient constraints; the validator returned a binary pass/fail plus detailed traces archived per episode. These archived traces (execution/scoring/*.json and execution/responses/*.txt) provide the empirical basis for the binary outcomes used in the analysis.

Preregistration→Execution reconciliation table. The concise juxtaposition below maps key preregistered values to the executed values and cites artifact evidence (paths and available SHA-256 hashes):

- benchmark_scope (preregistered): four OpenAlex targets: https://openalex.org/W7157506260, https://openalex.org/W4404602270, https://openalex.org/W4404534210, https://openalex.org/W7166900660 (listed in preregistration artifact; preregistration SHA-256 = 9a5e11c5b2b1c14c2a4a874a7ad0b9f215f8477a7becf4eb6dd1c0ff6a00ae7a).
- sampled_items (executed): provenance-stable synthetic tasks (source_identifier prefix "synthetic-netops:"); evidence: execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA-256 = b7c08599e3f96d8d5605a18f8f973e0707d7224327eeed7bde78c0d34cb83e55).
- planned_maximum_model_calls (preregistered): 300; executed model_calls_used: 150; evidence: execution manifest (execution/model_configuration.json SHA-256 = a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820; execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA-256 = 5337998d1d86aca507f77659d75cc9487cf3d87a157ed5044b8a9d5ff79b5586; deterministic_reconciliation artifact archived).
- independent_condition_generation (preregistered allowed): true allowed; executed = false (shared_initial_candidate semantics); evidence: execution/model_configuration.json (SHA-256 = a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820).
- contamination detector persistence (preregistered): persist full per-item overlap scores; executed: persist only upon threshold crossings or replacements; evidence: transformation manifest path execution/transformation_manifest.json recorded in execution summary (full hash manifest available in execution bundle).

Analysis executor and artifacts. The primary analysis executor paired_binary_analysis_v1 was used as preregistered; confirmatory outputs and contingency table are archived (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA-256 = c2ba9cdb5d0938eae910129ba511eadf309319e6e05b36d9e3b4860032deb80e; analysis/condition_summary.csv SHA-256 = 9d3de16521f01d53c002b69512a6edc0253a8953e413faeed5d1c0feb3e6d4f9). All cited artifact paths and available SHA-256 hashes are present in the execution bundle.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and primary outcomes. Execution completed planned_episode_count = 300 episodes (150 item pairs) with completed_episode_count = 300 and failed_episode_count = 0. Because independent_condition_generation = false and no high-confidence exclusions occurred, the pipeline used model_calls_used = 150 (one shared generation per item) rather than two separate generations per condition; provider call accounting and deterministic_reconciliation artifacts confirm these counts (see execution/model_configuration.json SHA-256 = a40e96e2...).

Contamination detector outcomes. The preregistered detectors produced zero high-confidence contamination flags in the executed sample; analysis/contamination_summary.csv contains no flagged rows (SHA-256 = 389227f0...). Because no items met the high-confidence threshold, the detector workflow did not persist a global per-item overlap table per the implemented persistence policy (recorded in the transformation manifest). We therefore report the artifact-documented absence of high-confidence flags and the consequent absence of an archived per-item overlap distribution for this run.

Validator outcomes and confirmatory statistics. The deterministic_netops_validator_v5 returned pass for all baseline episodes (baseline_success_count = 150/150; baseline_success_rate = 1.0) and for all guarded episodes (guarded_success_count = 150/150; guarded_success_rate = 1.0). The paired contingency table is n11 = 150, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA-256 = c2ba9cdb...). The primary estimand (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline) = 0.0 percentage points. Paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.0]. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. These numbers are reported exactly from archived analysis artifacts (analysis/* files) and per-episode validator traces (execution/scoring/*.json).

Representative episode diagnostic. Representative archived episode pair-000001 (execution/responses/task-000001-*.txt and execution/scoring/task-000001-*.json; provider trace and validator trace archived) illustrates the structure: normalized_response identical to reference; validator parsed_command_count = 4, required_command_count = 4, score = 1 (VALID_CONFIGURATION). The raw response artifact is execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt (SHA-256 = 8f38c8be...).

Interpretation: primary estimand untestable under executed semantics. The primary confirmatory estimand was prespecified to detect a reduction in validator pass rates due to guarded exclusions on contaminated items. Under the executed shared_initial_candidate semantics and provenance-stable synthetic sampling, baseline and guarded episodes reused identical model outputs when no exclusions occurred; thus the paired test is mechanically unable to observe generation-level discordance. We therefore classify the primary estimand as degenerate/untestable for detection of generation-level contamination in this executed run. The reported p-value and CI correctly reflect the observed concordance but do not provide evidence about contamination prevalence in independently generated public benchmarks.
sections.discussion:
Artifact-grounded diagnosis of degeneracy. Two archived execution facts explain the degenerate null result: (1) the confirmatory sample was drawn from a deterministic synthetic generator and labeled with source_identifier values beginning with "synthetic-netops:" (see execution/task_manifest.jsonl, SHA-256 = b7c08599...), and (2) the model configuration set independent_condition_generation = false (execution/model_configuration.json, SHA-256 = a40e96e2...), causing a single shared generation per item to be reused for both baseline and guarded episodes when no exclusions occurred. These artifacts jointly removed the possibility of generation-level discordance and therefore rendered the paired hypothesis untestable in practice.

Detector persistence tradeoffs and missing overlap summaries. The implemented detector saved detailed per-item fuzzy-overlap outputs only when threshold crossings or replacements occurred (documented in the transformation manifest execution/transformation_manifest.json). Because no high-confidence flags occurred, no per-item overlap table was persisted; this is an explicit artifact behavior rather than an omission. The practical consequence is reduced post-hoc interpretability: the archive does not contain per-item overlap distances that would indicate how close items were to the high-confidence threshold. To improve interpretability, future runs should persist full per-item overlap scores to enable threshold-sensitivity analysis.

Sensitivity and power implications (artifact-anchored). The preregistration's power guidance shows that detecting modest paired differences (e.g., 4–6 percentage points) requires independent generation events per condition and/or increased sample size and/or multi-model replication. The executed design used shared generation semantics and a single model, which materially reduces expected discordance even when contamination/paraphrase leakage is present; the archived paired_bootstrap CI and McNemar p-value correctly reflect this design choice. For contamination audits of public benchmarks we recommend: (a) sample provenance-rich public items, (b) set independent_condition_generation = true so baseline and guarded outputs are independently realized, (c) persist full per-item overlap scores, (d) expand to multiple model instances and seeds, and (e) add paraphrase-sensitive detectors plus human adjudication for borderline items. Each recommendation follows from explicit gaps visible in the execution artifacts (model_calls_used = 150; empty analysis/contamination_summary.csv; absence of per-item overlap table).

Operational implications and cautious generalization. The archival record confirms that deterministic validator oracles remain valuable: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 produced consistent traces confirming functional correctness on archived episodes. However, auditors must not generalize the synthetic shared-generation null to public benchmarks. The present artifacts support only the narrow inference that under deterministic synthetic sampling and shared generation semantics the preregistered conservative detectors produced no high-confidence flags and the guarded policy had no effect. They do not inform prevalence of contamination in web-sourced corpora or the effectiveness of paraphrase-robust detectors.
sections.conclusion: We conducted a fully preregistered, artifact-anchored paired audit of conservative contamination detectors for LLM-for-NetOps evaluation. In the reproducible 150-pair synthetic sample we observed zero preregistered high-confidence flags and identical validator pass rates (150/150 baseline, 150/150 guarded). The degenerate null outcome is artifact-supported and stems from provenance-stable synthetic sampling and shared_initial_candidate semantics; it does not imply absence of contamination in web-sourced benchmarks or failure of the detectors under different sampling regimes. We provide an explicit preregistration→execution reconciliation, confirm deterministic reconciliation checks passed, and recommend concrete design changes—provenance-rich public sampling, independent generation per condition, full per-item overlap persistence, multi-model replication, and paraphrase-robust detectors—to increase audit sensitivity. All experiment artifacts, validator traces, analysis inputs/outputs, and execution manifests are archived and are referenced in the Disclosure Statement below.

limitations: Single-model execution (gpt-5-mini) — results do not generalize across other LLM families, sizes, or training corpora.

The executed sample used provenance-stable synthetic/deterministically generated tasks (source_identifier prefix "synthetic-netops:") for this run; absence of preregistered high-confidence flags here may not reflect contamination prevalence in real-world, web-crawled benchmarks (the preregistration had targeted four public OpenAlex datasets).

Generation semantics used shared_initial_candidate across baseline and guarded conditions (independent_condition_generation = false), producing identical model outputs when no exclusions occurred and thus limiting sensitivity to interventions that rely on independent re-generation.

Contamination detection relied on preregistered conservative heuristics (exact match and fuzzy 5-gram overlap thresholds); subtler contamination patterns (paraphrased memorization, partial leakage) may escape these heuristics and require richer provenance, paraphrase-robust detectors, or human adjudication.

Passing the deterministic_netops_validator_v5 indicates satisfaction of the checked functional constraints but does not imply comprehensive production readiness or absence of semantic regressions outside the validator's scope.
